# Joint critical-cap profiles, exact two-cap accounting, and centroid slopes

These are joint constraints on one family of actual ambient caps. They
are not a proof of general three-fiber OC and do not assert existence of
a favorable centroid selector or deformation.

Let A,K,B be positive d-dimensional convex bodies at integer bases
-1,0,1, with (A+B)/2 subset K. Write their volumes a,c,b and M=a+c+b,
and Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d. Fix an actual source (0,y). Suppose caps

    H_i={u_i.(x-y)+beta_i z>=0}, u_i nonzero,

attain its raw depth Q. Put U_i=|A intersect (H_i)_-1|,
q_i=|K intersect (H_i)_0|, V_i=|B intersect (H_i)_1|. Thus

    U_i+q_i+V_i=Q.                                      (1)

Assume positive weights lambda_i satisfy sum lambda_i u_i=0 and put
Delta=sum lambda_i beta_i. The middle traces cover all R^d. If
Delta<=0 the A traces also cover; if Delta>=0 the B traces also cover.
This follows by summing actual signed margins, obtaining z Delta.
Relabel endpoints where appropriate so the additional covered endpoint
below is A. Every statement retains the actual different endpoint cut
offsets and the original halfspaces.

## 1. The ordinary profile, with its complete trimming proof

If halfspaces with cap volumes t_i cover a d-dimensional convex body D
of volume W, then for every alpha>=0,

    sum_i(t_i-alpha)_+ + alpha/Gamma >= W.                (2)

If W-sum(t_i-alpha)_+<=0 this is immediate. Otherwise remove from each
cap with t_i>alpha a distal parallel cap of mass t_i-alpha. Continuous
ordinary cap-volume tails give finite thresholds. Their retained
intersection with D is compact and convex and has positive volume at
least W-sum(t_i-alpha)_+. Each original cap has retained volume at most
alpha. The retained body's ordinary centroid belongs to one original
cap because the family covers D. Ordinary Grünbaum therefore bounds the
retained volume by alpha/Gamma. This proves (2). Boundary planes have
zero d-volume; alpha=0 is handled by the same contradiction or the
immediate nonpositive-remainder branch.

## 2. A joint profile retaining both dispersion and cross-capture

For every tau in [0,Q], apply (2) to K at alpha=tau and to A at
alpha=Q-tau. Using (1) gives

    Q/Gamma + sum_i |q_i-tau|
       >= c+a + sum_i min{V_i,(tau-q_i)_+}.              (3)

Indeed the summand from the two profiles is

    (q_i-tau)_+ +(tau-q_i-V_i)_+
       =|q_i-tau|-min{V_i,(tau-q_i)_+}.

Equivalently,

    Q/Gamma + sum_i dist(tau,[q_i,q_i+V_i]) >= c+a.      (4)

These are identities and inequalities for the same caps. No independent
fiber cap ordering or allocation is substituted. The interval form
shows exactly where the unowned endpoint captures enter.

For three caps order q_1<=q_2<=q_3. Taking tau=q_2 gives the exact
necessary inequality

    q_3-q_1 >= c+a-Q/Gamma + min{V_1,q_2-q_1}.           (5)

Ties cause no ambiguity: when q_1=q_2 the cross term vanishes. Under
strict noheavy and Q<Gamma M/2, (5) implies

    q_3-q_1 > (c+a-b)/2 + min{V_1,q_2-q_1}.             (6)

Thus any hypothetical bad three-cap menu must have a definite spread
of its own-fiber cap masses, with an additional charge for the displayed
cross-capture. Equal own volumes are excluded without any BM-equality
assumption. Formula (3) is valid in every d and for any number of caps;
(5) is the three-cap specialization.

## 3. Exact two-cap overlap-minus-gap identity

Suppose the projected circuit has two caps. Rescale them positively to

    H_+: t+alpha z>=0, H_-: -t+beta z>=0,
    t=u.(x-y), u nonzero.

Put delta=alpha+beta. At z=0 their traces partition K up to a null
boundary. If delta>0, B is covered and A may have an uncovered gap.
Let J_B be the volume in B of the intersection interval
- alpha<=t<=beta, and let G_A be the volume in A of the gap
- beta<t<alpha. Then exact inclusion-exclusion gives

    2Q=M+J_B-G_A.                                      (7)

If delta<0 the roles reverse, with the corresponding intersection and
gap. If delta=0 both fibers are partitioned and 2Q=M. Hence always

    Q >= [M-max(a,b)]/2.                               (8)

Under noheavy, (8) gives Q>=M/4>=Gamma M/2; the last comparison is
strict when d>=2. Thus a below-OC middle source cannot have a two-cap
projected circuit. All endpoint boundary planes are d-volume null;
purely integer halfspaces are still controlled by Q's definition.

## 4. Centroid separation under a hypothetical failure

Assume strict noheavy and Q<Gamma M/2. Let g_A,g,g_B be the ordinary
centroids and put m=(g_A+g_B)/2 in K. No critical cap can contain two
of the three lifted centroids: their distinct fibers contribute at
least Gamma times their combined volume, which exceeds Gamma M/2.
In particular every critical cap containing (0,g) misses both endpoint
centroids strictly. Its own capture satisfies q_i>=Gamma c, while

    U_i+V_i=Q-q_i<Gamma min(a,b).                       (9)

The last inequality uses M/2<c+min(a,b), which is strict noheavy.
Conversely any critical cap containing an endpoint centroid has
q_i<Gamma c and misses (0,g) strictly.

For a nonzero normal u define the finite positive coarea-density bound

    S_D(u)=sup_t H_(d-1)(D intersect {u.x=t})/|u|.

Fubini gives the elementary quantitative fact: if the actual cap of D
has mass w<Gamma|D|, its centroid lies strictly outside, and its signed
functional gap to the cut is at least

    (Gamma|D|-w)/S_D(u).                               (10)

To prove it, compare the actual cap with its parallel cap through the
ordinary centroid, which has mass at least Gamma|D|. Their difference
is a slab of functional thickness equal to that centroid gap, and its
volume is at most S_D(u) times the thickness. No section differentiability
or proper-boundary continuity is required.

Let I_0 be the critical caps containing the middle centroid. It is
nonempty by the middle cover. For i in I_0, the two negative endpoint
centroid margins and (10) give

    -2u_i.(m-y)
       >= (Gamma a-U_i)/S_A(u_i)
             +(Gamma b-V_i)/S_B(u_i)>0.

Since u_i.(g-y)>=0,

    -u_i.(m-g)
       >= (1/2)[(Gamma a-U_i)/S_A(u_i)
                    +(Gamma b-V_i)/S_B(u_i)].          (11)

Thus these genuinely unfavorable slopes along the centroid-difference
vector have explicit positive mass-deficit lower bounds.

## 5. Exact drift and compensation identities

Define the three functional centroid margins

    l_i^- =u_i.(g_A-y)-beta_i,
    l_i^0 =u_i.(g-y),
    l_i^+ =u_i.(g_B-y)+beta_i.

Continuous balance gives exactly

    sum lambda_i l_i^-=-Delta,
    sum lambda_i l_i^0=0,
    sum lambda_i l_i^+=Delta.                          (12)

Let P_- and P_+ be sums of lambda_i(l_i^-)_+ and
lambda_i(l_i^+)_+, respectively. Equations (9)--(12) imply

    P_- >= [sum_(i in I_0) lambda_i
                       (Gamma a-U_i)/S_A(u_i)-Delta]_+,
    P_+ >= [sum_(i in I_0) lambda_i
                       (Gamma b-V_i)/S_B(u_i)+Delta]_+. (13)

Adding the exact positive-minus-negative identities in (12), so that
Delta cancels, gives

    P_-+P_+ >= sum_(i in I_0) lambda_i
          [(Gamma a-U_i)/S_A(u_i)
                    +(Gamma b-V_i)/S_B(u_i)].          (14)

Likewise sum lambda_i u_i.(m-g)=0, so (11) forces compensating positive
slopes:

    sum_(u_i.(m-g)>0) lambda_i u_i.(m-g)
       >= (1/2)sum_(i in I_0) lambda_i
          [(Gamma a-U_i)/S_A(u_i)
                    +(Gamma b-V_i)/S_B(u_i)].          (15)

These identities retain the signed integer drift and actual section
scales. They do not say that the compensating slopes are small or that
one motion toward g or m improves every cap. Positive normal balance
itself prohibits a common strictly favorable first-order direction.

## 6. Actual obstruction to automatic double-centroid matching

The stronger claim that every genuine critical cap circuit must contain
a cap holding two fiber centroids is false, even with strict noheavy,
rank-two projected normals, and a global deepest middle source.
Use the already proved source
`candidate 907b6bf347e73ada`, with

    l=1, c_parameter=9/20, L=[-1/2,1/2],
    C={-1<=z<=1, -1<=x<=1+(9/5)(1-|z|), w in L}.

Its fiber areas are 2,19/5,2; its exact global raw depth is Q=69/20 at
Y=(0,9/20,0). The all-direction proof is the exact paired-tail argument
in that source, including every oblique continuous padding direction.
The three genuinely critical caps are

    H_0: x>=9/20,
    H_+: x<=9/20+2z+w/2,
    H_-: x<=9/20-2z-w/2.

Their margins obey 2L_0+L_++L_-=0, so Delta=0 and they cover all three
fibers. Their cap-area table is

                H_0       H_+       H_-
    A          11/20       0          2
    K          47/20      29/20      29/20
    B          11/20       2          0.

The continuous centroids are g_A=g_B=(0,0), g=(9/10,0). Their signed
margin table is

                H_0       H_+       H_-
    g_A        -9/20     -31/20      49/20
    g           9/20      -9/20      -9/20
    g_B        -9/20      49/20     -31/20.

Each critical cap therefore contains exactly one lifted fiber centroid.
This is an actual geometric obstruction to automatic centroid matching,
not an arbitrary sign matrix. The middle-centroid cap has root deficit
1-sqrt(11/47)>1/3 in d=2. The source satisfies OC with considerable
room, so it does not contradict the necessary consequences (9)--(15)
under a hypothetical below-OC budget.

The exact polynomial overlap-profile obstruction in the archived source
also shows why an ordinary one-body profile cannot simply be imposed on
the three global cap masses. In (3)--(4) the dispersion and cross-capture
terms have therefore been retained explicitly.
